messages:
From: Jane Park <security@finedge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 scope question — hosted/dedicated/private

Hi Sofia,

We're preparing for FinEdge's upcoming vendor audit and need to confirm the scope for Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report. Specifically: which hosting modes are covered as "in-scope" for the standard report period Oct 1, 2025 — Sep 30, 2026? Our audit team has asked whether: 

- Shared/hosted API endpoints are covered (we assume yes)
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) instances under Redwood Dedicated are included by default
- Private/VPC or customer-managed on-prem deployments are in-scope or require a separate bridge letter or attestation

Could you also provide a redacted copy of your latest SOC 2 Type II and, if applicable, a bridge letter template we can present to our auditors? If you have a simple matrix that maps hosting mode -> in-scope/covered controls, that would be very helpful.

Timing: our audit kickoff is week of 2027-05-03, so if possible we'd like materials by 2027-04-25.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Director, Vendor Security
FinEdge Payments

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question — hosted/dedicated/private

Thanks for the clear ask, Jane — good timing. Short answers up front:

- Hosted (shared API): IN SCOPE for our SOC 2 Type II (standard report).
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): typically IN SCOPE when the customer is using Redwood Dedicated with Redwood-managed control plane and pools are within the scope period; there are tenancy/contract nuances we should confirm.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: generally OUT OF SCOPE for the hosted SOC 2 report unless you have contracted Redwood Private with the managed control plane option AND requested inclusion during the audit period — in that case we provide a bridge letter or scoped attestation.

I'm attaching a short matrix and will follow up with Marissa and Rishi to prepare the redacted SOC 2 PDF and a bridge-letter draft you can share with your auditors.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Wed 2027-04-20 to walk the audit team through the matrix and confirm whether FinEdge's Dedicated pools (if any) were under committed capacity during the audit period.

What I'm sending:
- Redwood_SOC2-TypeII_2026_redacted.pdf (redacted copy of the auditor's report covering 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30)
- redwood-bridge-letter-proposed-20270418.docx (draft bridge letter that explains the default scope boundaries and options for inclusion)
- hosting-scope-matrix-brief.pdf (same matrix Sofia referenced)

Quick notes from our side:
- Hosted API endpoints are fully covered by the SOC 2 Type II report.
- Redwood Dedicated is usually covered if the customer uses Redwood-managed Dedicated pools and the pools were in a committed configuration during the audit period — if a customer self-manages control plane components in their VPC or on-prem, those components are out of scope.
- Private/VPC and on-prem deployments are out-of-scope for the standard report unless the customer has purchased Redwood Private with managed-control-plane and we included it in our audit scope. For customers that need an attestation, the bridge letter explains what was reviewed and recommends language auditors can accept.

If FinEdge needs the bridge letter signed on company letterhead or a notarized addendum for their procurement team, let me know and we'll route to legal for sign-off.
